name: Jawbreaker
label: Tupelo
lede: Three guys from Santa Monica who swore off major labels, signed for a million dollars and watched their fans turn their backs on the record, then got a second chance at Riot Fest.

eras.title: Rise, then Jawbreaker
eras.text: Two Santa Monica friends land at NYU, answer a bass player's flyer and spend two years as a band called Rise with the wrong singers. By 1989 they have a new name, a new frontman and a first show in Los Angeles.

years.h: Two Santa Monica friends answer a bassist's flyer in New York
years.p: [[Blake Schwarzenbach|c7d68007-b688-426f-a496-08467a0a6f44]] and [[Adam Pfahler|27a4001b-d621-40a6-aab8-6dd181b016ac]] move east for NYU and meet Chris Bauermeister through a flyer he posted. They rehearse at Giant Studios on Sixth Avenue as a band called Rise.
years.xp: Rise ran through several vocalists before Schwarzenbach wrote and sang a song called "Shield Your Eyes" for a demo. Jon Liu, an earlier singer, later said that was the song where everything worked.

years.h: Rise move to Los Angeles and hand the mic to Jon Liu
years.p: The band relocates west in fall 1987 with Liu as lead vocalist. It lasts until Schwarzenbach takes over the singing.

years.h: Rise become Jawbreaker, and Schwarzenbach starts singing
years.p: With the new name comes a new arrangement: Schwarzenbach as the primary vocalist for good.

years.cap: Jawbreaker reunion at Riot Fest 2017, Chicago · Wikimedia
years.h: First show as Jawbreaker: Club 88, Los Angeles
years.p: The trio plays its first live show as Jawbreaker at Club 88 on March 16, 1989.

eras.title: Unfun, a broken-up tour and the Mission
eras.text: A two-day debut, a summer of van misery, a move to San Francisco and a record made while Blake's voice was failing. This is where the band becomes the band.

years.h: Unfun: recorded in two days in Venice, California
years.p: Cut in January 1990 and released in May on Shredder Records (SH-07). It is the debut album, and the sound of three people who had rehearsed a lot and recorded very little.
years.xp: Adam Pfahler reissued a remastered Unfun on his own Blackball Records on March 30, 2010.

years.cap: Blake Schwarzenbach with Jawbreaker at The Fillmore, SF, 2022 · Wikimedia
years.h: The "Fuck 90" tour: two months in a van and a breakup announced
years.p: Touring with Econochrist, Bauermeister stops speaking to the other two when they reach Canada, and by the end the band says it is done.
years.xp:
Schwarzenbach later put the whole tour in numbers: about six great shows, and maybe 25 forgettable ones in the kind of metal club you find in Florida.

Schwarzenbach and Bauermeister went back to NYU, and Pfahler regretted the split. The three eventually made up in New York.

years.h: They move to San Francisco, across the hall from Lance Hahn
years.p: The band settles in the Mission District; Pfahler and Schwarzenbach share an apartment across from Bauermeister and [[J Church|bad96c62-50f8-4159-b155-3ffb63c698f8]]'s Lance Hahn, and local bands [[Econochrist|bcaa3d82-4ac7-4977-a202-af30cc22c12a]] and [[Samiam|787aa69f-f419-4e24-8c13-33511a20428d]] adopt them.

years.h: "Kiss the Bottle" arrives on the 17 Reasons Mission compilation
years.p: It is the last song Schwarzenbach records before throat surgery, and the vocal shows it. It is a portrait of the drinkers outside a Mission liquor store.
years.xp: Andy Greenwald, in Nothing Feels Good, calls it one of the band's best-loved songs, a working-class anthem with a steady heart. Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta has named it a favorite.

years.h: Bivouac: the record where they stretch out
years.p: Recorded with engineer Billy Anderson and released on Tupelo and Communion (TUP 38). Pfahler says the band was trying to prove something and stretching out.

years.cap: Blake Schwarzenbach with Jets to Brazil, Santa Cruz, 2001 · Wikimedia
years.h: Throat polyps, a European tour and surgery in Ireland
years.p: Schwarzenbach starts losing his voice onstage as Bivouac comes out. In Ireland it gets worse and he has surgery; the tour resumes a week later.
years.xp: He has described every day of that tour as full of dread, standing up there to see what would happen.

eras.title: Chicago, Steve Albini and a cat
eras.text: Two records for the indie label Tupelo, an Albini session credited to his cat, Nirvana dates that draw label interest, and the DGC deal that follows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jawbreaker (band) · mxdwn: Steve Albini Admits Confusing Jawbreaker with Jawbox in Teaser for Upcoming Documentary
years.h: Steve Albini records them in Chicago. The credit goes to his cat
years.p: Most of 24 Hour Revenge Therapy is cut in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], officially credited to Fluss, his cat. Three more tracks follow in August with Billy Anderson in San Francisco.
years.xp: Albini later appears in the teaser for the Jawbreaker documentary, where he admits confusing Jawbreaker with Jawbox.

years.h: They open six dates on Nirvana's In Utero tour
years.p: The dates put Jawbreaker in front of thousands and set the rumor mill going: someone from a label sees them and they get snapped up.
years.xp: Pfahler says people really came down on the band for going on tour with Nirvana. The prediction turned out right.

years.h: 24 Hour Revenge Therapy comes out on Tupelo
years.p: Released as Tupelo TUP 49 and Communion COMM 49. Andy Greenwald calls it arguably the band's best, Replacements-style regret set to Gilman Street speed.

years.h: After Warner, Capitol and DGC meetings, they sign with DGC
years.p: The deal is said to be worth $1 million, and it turns on A&R man Mark Kates, who met them on the Nirvana tour and kept in touch.
years.xp: Ben Weasel of Screeching Weasel had promised to eat his hat if Jawbreaker ever signed to a major. He published a photo of himself doing it in Maximumrocknroll.

eras.title: A million dollars and a turned back
eras.text: The band that swore off major labels signs to DGC and gets the reaction it feared, from crowds who sit down at its own shows. It lasts about ten months from release to the last van.

years.h: Rob Cavallo takes over: Fantasy Studios, six weeks of guitar takes
years.p: Cavallo, fresh off Green Day's Dookie, has Bauermeister and Pfahler done in three days. Schwarzenbach then spends six weeks on 12-hour days with him.
years.xp: Cavallo said Schwarzenbach really wanted to be heard, and decided to sing differently. Cavallo thought the songs could use some precision.

q: Pretty chilling. Like a muted acknowledgment.
years.src: Uproxx: Jawbreaker's Blake Schwarzenbach On 'Dear You' And Touring · Wikipedia: Dear You
years.h: Dear You: fans hear a voice sanded down
years.p: DGC 24831, produced by Cavallo. The clear vocals and glossy guitars divide the fans who had trusted Schwarzenbach with their private lives.
years.xp: Schwarzenbach later called the label's response pretty chilling, like a muted acknowledgment. DGC gave feedback, he said, where selling 50,000 copies meant nobody would say anything.

years.h: "Fireman" video: three men in a tiny room, MTV airs it eight times
years.p: [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] director Mark Kohr shoots it at the Fox Oakland. Mark Kates blamed the band's lack of visual appeal.

years.h: Flyers on the "Monsters of Jaw" tour with Jawbox
years.p: Activist Brian Zero hands out anti-Jawbreaker flyers, and some crowds sit down or turn their backs on Dear You songs.
years.xp: Kates recalled the Roxy headline show, with kids on the floor and their backs to the stage during the new songs. Samiam's Sergie Loobkoff called a Warfield show in San Francisco a turning point: it was like no one cared.

years.h: Bauermeister and Schwarzenbach fight on a sidewalk in Salem, Oregon
years.p: By then the two travel in separate vans. It comes to a physical fight in Salem, which spills onto the street.
years.xp: Bauermeister remembered shouting at Schwarzenbach that he was a stupid son of a bitch who thinks it is all about him.

years.h: Jawbreaker announce the breakup on the Fourth of July
years.p: The band ends after a run of unhappy dates behind Dear You, about ten months after the album came out.

eras.title: Jets to Brazil and a video store
eras.text: Schwarzenbach goes to Brooklyn and Jets to Brazil, Pfahler opens a video store and a record label, and Dear You comes back into print.

years.h: Schwarzenbach fronts Jets to Brazil in Brooklyn
years.p: [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]] mixes Britpop and piano ballads, and gets "unspeakably scathing" reviews from critics still fixated on his Jawbreaker legacy.

years.h: Pfahler opens Lost Weekend Video and starts Blackball Records
years.p: He stays in the Mission and plays in J Church with Lance Hahn from 1998 to 2002. Bauermeister goes back to his toy store job. Pfahler runs the Jawbreaker catalog through Blackball.

years.h: Live 4/30/96: the last tour, on record
years.p: Recorded on April 30, 1996 and released by Pfahler on Blackball as BB-002.

years.h: Pfahler buys back Dear You for $10,000 and reissues it
years.p: He licenses the album from Universal for ten years and Blackball puts it out as a double LP with bonus tracks including "Shirt." It had been selling for double its retail price.

years.h: First time in a room in 11 years: three songs, no cameras
years.p: The Don't Break Down filmmakers get all three together in a San Francisco studio. They play "Bivouac," "Condition Oakland" and "Parabola" and the audio is recorded off the board.
years.xp: The band chose not to film it, out of respect for the sanctity of the moment and fear that they would suck, according to the account of the session.

eras.title: The reunion Blake said would never happen
eras.text: He said it for years: he physically could not sing those songs. Then a festival slot, a documentary and Brooklyn Steel.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jawbreaker (band) · The FADER: After 21 Years, Jawbreaker Is Reuniting To Headline Riot Fest
years.h: Riot Fest announces Jawbreaker as a surprise headliner
years.p: The announcement comes after years of reunion denials from Schwarzenbach. Pfahler and Bauermeister had said they would do it any time.
years.xp: Schwarzenbach had said he did not think he could sing the songs. Pfahler said he would do it in a heartbeat.

yt: Condition Oakland, first show in 21 years
years.h: First reunion show in 21 years: Ivy Room, Albany, California
years.p: A private show opening for Monsula. Fan video of the set is online.

years.src: Stereogum: At Riot Fest 2017, Jawbreaker Finally Became Rock Stars
years.h: Riot Fest 2017: Jawbreaker headline the final night
years.p: They open with "Boxcar" and close with "Bivouac." Schwarzenbach tells the crowd to call in to work tomorrow for a general strike.
years.xp:
Stereogum's account has the crowd enormous for a band without radio hits, if smaller than Nine Inch Nails and Wu-Tang Clan. Schwarzenbach tore the monitor off and mangled his guitar in the finale, while Pfahler threw his sticks into the crowd.

Fans singing along on the choruses were caught on the video screens.

years.h: Brooklyn Steel sells out three nights, the first New York shows in 25 years
years.p: The run follows two San Francisco dates in January; the Hollywood Palladium follows in March, their first LA shows in 22 years.

years.h: At the Fillmore they play "Gemini", written after Dear You, never recorded
years.p: They also debut "Black Art," a rearranged Thorns of Life song, across a three-night San Francisco residency.

years.h: First European tour in 25 years, ending in Barcelona
years.p: They also play Groezrock, Primavera Sound and London's Shepherd's Bush Empire, with Beach Slang supporting on two dates.
years.xp: At a 2019 documentary Q&A at Nitehawk in New York the band said writing a new 7-inch was slow, with Bauermeister in Olympia, Pfahler in San Francisco and Schwarzenbach in Brooklyn.

years.src: Uproxx: Jawbreaker's Blake Schwarzenbach On 'Dear You' And Touring
years.h: Dear You anniversary tour plays the album in full
years.p: A 27-date run with songs the band had not played live before, including "Oyster" and "Unlisted."
